trajectory_summary: The call opened with strong customer engagement and a rich, voluntary disclosure of pain points (roof, bill, self-sufficiency interest) that the rep mostly let breathe. But the rep then walked past several enthusiasm signals, engaged in unsolicited scope creep on the neighbor's system, never flipped the captured bill or interest reason into forward momentum, and ended the call abruptly on a utility DQ without exhausting options or committing to next steps. Energy that was built in the first two minutes leaked out entirely by the end.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear; based on transcript this is clearly a dq (or at minimum no_appointment) - the rep explicitly states Edisto may not be workable and ends the call with only a vague 'I'll give you a callback' with no time attached, which does not meet the callback bar of a stated time.

observed_outcome.quote: it just looks like we might not be able to help you at the moment
observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep ends the call on a probable utility/net-metering DQ with only a vague promise to call back if the design team can help - no date, no time, and no appointment was set.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Rep captured '$2.50' as the bill at 04:19 and acknowledged it ('About $2.50. Perfect.') but never tied it back to the customer's own stated pain ('electric bill's kinda high') before the call moved to the utility qualifier and then ended on a DQ.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep asked for the average bill but never raised collecting the actual utility bill or requested a photo/email/text of the bill.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: And my wife and I are looking at having to spend money on a roof right now, and our electric bill's kinda high.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: Customer's stated reason (roof cost pressure plus high electric bill, and interest in self-sufficiency/backup power) was acknowledged with 'those are all good concerns to have' at 02:28 but never reinforced again or tied to any next step before the call ended.
